newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher on improving economy.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher on improving economy.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Saturday after the government's announcement on Friday that the island's economy had improved in November, brokers said.
The weighted index closed up 40.88 points, or 0.60 percent, at 6,903.90.
Turnover was an active T$36.26 billion in Saturday's abbreviated session.

The Council for Economic Planning and Development said on Friday that the economy improved to a "green light" condition in November, indicating possible recovery from October's "yellow blue light", which indicated a possible slowdown.
"The anouncement was somewhat a positive boost, triggering some buying after two previous falling sessions," said Allen Huang, a securities manager for National Securities.
"But it was not enough to break the market out of consolidation," Huang added.
Many analysts have expected Taiwan's economy to gradually recover in the fourth quarter of 1996, spurred by improving export orders and industrial output.
Electronics, seen as Taiwan's most fundamentally sound sector, rose 1.26 percent with Ritek Incorp gaining the daily seven-percent limit or T$5 to T$77.
Brokers said the index would stay within a narrow range on Monday because many investors are expected to be on the sidelines before the upcoming New Year holiday.
"Investors generally are reluctant to buy or sell actively right before a new year, so the market likely will be quiet on Monday," Huang said.
